description: Staging trial of customer-side VPC flow-log aggregation (aws-core-tap#218), seed wave 5 (tools/seed/wave5-flowlogs) in the GovCloud staging account, us-gov-west-1, under the seeder identity; the collector took no part. Counts, codes and booleans only; hosts are named by role (client, server), no account number, resource id or message.
time_box: applied 02:39:38Z, destroyed 03:10:05Z (31 minutes of a 2-hour box)
verdict: pass: flow logs, Glue partition projection, the summarising query with each filter, and the scheduled path all worked; two design defects found (below)

checks.plan creates only this run's resources: 22 to create, 0 to change or destroy
checks.flow logs arrive as hourly Parquet under: first object 5 minutes after apply, at .../aws-region=us-gov-west-1/year=2026/month=11/day=10/hour=02/
checks.unfiltered summary: SUCCEEDED, 2,217 bytes scanned, 160 s; 10 rows; client and server addresses and the server ports 8080, 9090, 9443 all right; 9443 REJECT on the server's interface, as the security group intends
checks.host filter (server interface): SUCCEEDED; 5 rows, every one on the server's interface
checks.port filter (8080, 9443): SUCCEEDED; 6 rows, only those ports, ACCEPT and REJECT both present
checks.fixed window (3 minutes): SUCCEEDED, 326 bytes scanned; rows only for records starting inside the window
checks.scheduled path (EventBridge Scheduler ca: a scheduled run SUCCEEDED and wrote its summary, so the role's Athena, Glue and S3 permissions hold
checks.output format: INSERT INTO the JSON table wrote gzipped JSON lines (.gz), readable without a Parquet library
checks.destroy and leftovers: 22 destroyed; VPC, flow log, buckets, workgroup, Glue database, role and schedule gone; the tagging API still listed 8 deleted entries (2 terminated instances, 2 volumes, 3 security-group rules, the flow log), each confirmed gone or terminated by a direct describe

findings: Each conversation appears 4 times (2 interfaces x 2 directions): a reader must merge them on (client, server, port, protocol).

syn_seen (any SYN bit in the record) was true on every row, so it cannot name the initiator; prior art (the AWS flow-log record examples) says a record whose flags have SYN without ACK (2 or 3, not 18 or 19) is the initiator's direction. The query used the lower-port rule, which was right here.

A one-minute schedule with ~160 s queries overlapped: 1 of the scheduled runs failed with HIVE_S3_THROTTLING and later ones queued; AWS warns overlapping INSERT INTO runs can duplicate partitions. Runs must be serialised and idempotent, and the window must lag the clock for late delivery (about 10 minutes).
not_checked: the collector side (reading summaries onto the grid): not built yet
volume beyond two instances; cost was not measured, only estimated in cost.md
flow-log fields newer than the trial's format (pkt-src/dst-aws-service, next-hop-interface-id)
method: Each query was rendered from the live configuration with terraform console and the filter variables, run with aws athena start-query-execution in the wave's workgroup, and its output read back from S3. Output was scrubbed of 12-digit numbers and ARNs before it was read.

retrial.description: Re-trial after the prior-art fixes (aws-core-tap#218 comment 6757895267) and George's source, destination and pair filters: same wave, same account and identity, rewritten query (one row per conversation, flags decide the client, lagged hourly window, UNLOAD to an empty per-run prefix, newer fields).
retrial.time_box: applied 14:35:54Z, destroyed 15:47:47Z (72 minutes of a 2-hour box)
retrial.verdict: pass after one fix: every filter, the re-run refusal, the cross-interface count and the scheduled path worked; the first scheduled run failed on a module defect (below), fixed and re-run green

checks.plan creates only this run's resources: 21 to create, 0 to change or destroy (the named query is gone)
checks.newer flow-log fields in GovCloud: the flow log was accepted with pkt-src-aws-service, pkt-dst-aws-service and next-hop-interface-id (version 11) in its format; next-hop-interface-id arrived populated, naming the interface at the other end
checks.unfiltered, fixed window: SUCCEEDED; 3 conversations (8080 and 9090 ACCEPT, 9443 refused), every connection decided by flags
checks.filter_sources=client: SUCCEEDED; the same 3 conversations, each with the client as client
checks.filter_pairs server>client: SUCCEEDED; 0 rows and no object written, correct because the server never opens a connection to the client
checks.re-run with the same run time: FAILED as intended: HIVE_PATH_ALREADY_EXISTS, nothing written, the first run's object untouched
checks.counted once across both interfaces: port 8080 over 14:30-14:50: 35 connections, 12,145 bytes client to server and 25,200 back, exactly 35 x 347 and 35 x 720 in a raw per-record query; each connection appears on both interfaces
checks.scheduled path: the 15:25Z run FAILED (defect below); after the fix the 15:45Z run SUCCEEDED under the schedule's role and summarised the lagged window 14:00:00Z-15:00:00Z (61-62 connections per port, all decided by flags) into summaries/run=2026-11-10T15:45:00Z/
checks.destroy and leftovers: 21 destroyed; no role, buckets, workgroup, schedule or Glue database left; the tagging API still listed 8 deleted entries (2 terminated instances, 2 volumes, 3 security-group rules, the flow log), each confirmed gone or terminated by a direct describe

findings: Terraform jsonencode writes < and > as \u003c and \u003e, so the scheduler's <aws.scheduler.scheduled-time> keyword was hidden and Athena received the keyword itself (INVALID_FUNCTION_ARGUMENT). Fixed by restoring the two characters after encoding; the stored input then held no escapes and the next run passed.

A refused conversation reads action MIXED, not REJECT: the client's interface accepted each packet out and the server's interface rejected it. Accurate per hop; a reader wanting 'was it refused' should read rejected_records.
